responses.explanation: Correct: Todo.to_dict() read done twice (asdict(self), then is_overdue()), so a complete() landing between the two reads could make POST /todos answer done=false, overdue=false for a past-due todo. Fixed as the refutation condition (a) asks: to_dict() now takes one copy of the todo (dataclasses.replace) and builds both asdict() and overdue from that copy, so done is read once. The signatures in spec.interfaces are unchanged and the POST routes still call to_dict(); list_dicts keeps building under the lock. Regression test: test_post_response_stays_consistent_when_completed_while_it_is_built wraps app.storage.asdict so store.complete(1) runs right after the fields are read, which is the reviewer's window made deterministic. It asserts the hook fired and that overdue == not done for a 2000-01-01 todo. It fails on the round-1 head (done False, overdue False) and passes at e563e95. responses.explanation: Correct: with the clock patched in every pytest test and local-all inheriting a UTC environment, a today_utc() that used the host date passed the whole plan. I applied both suggested fixes. (a) test_today_utc_is_the_utc_date_not_the_host_date replaces app.storage.datetime with a datetime subclass pinned at 1999-12-31T23:30Z. Its now(tz) returns that instant in tz, and its naive now() returns UTC+10 wall time, which is already 2000-01-01. The test asserts storage.today_utc() == date(1999, 12, 31). The forbidden strings are avoided, so plan command 8 still passes. (b) local-all starts the server with a POSIX TZ whose calendar date differs from the UTC date at run time: UTC-12 before 12:00 UTC, else UTC+14. A server that judges by its local date then fails boundary, listing and overdue-list. Refutation-condition run, with TZ=UTC as on the orchestrator and on a clean clone of 93ced45: with `return date.today()` and again with `return datetime.now().date()`, pytest gives 1 failed, 38 passed (exit 1) and local-all gives 7 passed, 3 failed (exit 1). Unmodified HEAD gives 39 passed and 10 passed. rollover-local patches the clock, so it passes either way, which is expected.
